problems.text: A crew spreads 265 g of sodium chloride (NaCl) on the ice on a road. The salt dissolves in 1.50 kg of meltwater. Assuming complete dissociation and ideal solution behavior, what is the freezing point of the brine? For water, K_f = 1.86 °C·kg/mol.
problems.constants: K_f (water) = 1.86 °C·kg/mol: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, Table 11.2 (also Appendix E). Molar masses from Appendix A: Na 22.99, K 39.10, Mg 24.31, Ca 40.08, Cl 35.45 g/mol (Cl from the table figure; the extracted text omits it). NaCl = 58.44 g/mol. Ideal i = 2 (complete dissociation; ruling of 20 Oct).

problems.sim_reveal: The page draws freezing point against grams of this salt in the problem's meltwater (from 0 °C) and marks: pure water at 0 °C; the student's freezing point at the problem's grams; the student's prediction for twice the salt, beside the page's own point for it.

sim_instrument.text: Move `salt_g` until `Tf_readout` reads −10.0 °C. Checked value: 235.6 g; accept any whole number of grams from 235 to 236 (the grams at which `Tf_readout` shows −10.0).
